title: driver-info
description: Payload published retained by each Driver to renewvan/<driver>/info (three segments, so it is never mistaken for a four-segment entity topic). The Driver's manifest (driver-manifest.schema.json) plus a REQUIRED build-stamped version and OPTIONAL board_serial and ip. Published on every connect immediately before 'online' on renewvan/<driver>/health, and left retained when the Driver goes offline so consumers can show 'offline, last seen <version>'. Home Assistant field mapping, for anyone bridging Driver info to an HA device block (documented here only; nothing HA-shaped goes on the wire): product -> model, version -> sw_version, board_serial -> serial_number, homepage -> configuration_url, driver -> identifiers. board_serial is a support identity for display, never a join key, and every Driver on one Host publishes the same value. Formats seen so far: (1) a Raspberry Pi SoC serial, the Serial line of /proc/cpuinfo, 16 hex digits such as 10000000abcdef01; (2) an ESP32 MAC address as AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF. It is omitted, never faked or 'unknown', when it cannot be read or is empty or all zeros. ip is the Board's own current IPv4 address, for a Driver that runs on a Board with its own network address (an ESP32 on WiFi): it is as of the last connect, because info is republished on every connect, and it is omitted when the Driver has no address of its own to report (a Pi-side Driver does not publish it: the Pi's address is on renewvan/hub/status).

driver.description: The Driver's key; must equal the <driver> topic segment this payload is published under. A lowercase slug with no driver- prefix. The reserved key 'demo' is rejected: it is the Demo namespace root, never a Driver.

product.description: Human-readable product name shown as the Driver's title (Home Assistant: model).

source.description: What the Driver reads: the hardware or feed it senses or remaps.

publishes.description: Entity types the Driver publishes. Same static enum as driver-manifest.schema.json, kept in sync with the entity schemas by schema/validate-examples.sh.

manufacturer.description: Optional. Who makes the Driver. Consumers show 'renewvan' when Driver info exists without one.

homepage.description: Optional. Project or product URL (Home Assistant: configuration_url).

version.description: Build-stamped version (Home Assistant: sw_version): the git release tag for a Python Driver, the 'git describe --tags --always --dirty' string for the ESP32 relay, or the literal 'dev' when no version was stamped. Never read from the manifest.

board_serial.description: Optional. Serial of the Board the Driver runs on (Home Assistant: serial_number); free string, minimum length 1. See the schema description for the two formats seen. Omitted when unavailable.

ip.description: Optional. The Board's own current IPv4 address in dotted-quad form, e.g. the address DHCP gave an ESP32. Published only by a Driver that knows its own address; omitted, never '0.0.0.0' or a placeholder, when it has none yet. As of the moment info was published: info is republished on every connect, so the value is as fresh as the Driver's last (re)connect.
